 Pune Police Action Exposes ₹35 Lakh Robbery Case Suppression
 By UrbanAcres Editorial 
 October 29, 2026 
 0 
 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp 
 Pune Police have transferred the senior inspector of Market Yard police station after a ₹35 lakh robbery was recorded as a ₹1 lakh property theft case, prompting questions about how a serious crime was handled at the station level. Pune Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar described the recording of the incident as “suppression of crime” while speaking to the Times of India on Wednesday.
 The robbery took place on October 9 in the Market Yard police station jurisdiction. According to Kumar, the businessman involved visited the station several times to report that an Angadia carrying his cash had been robbed. Station staff, however, recorded the incident as a case of property missing instead of registering it as a robbery.
 The discrepancy came to light during a separate investigation by Swargate police. On Tuesday, officers arrested two suspects in connection with an attempted robbery reported on September 23. The incident involved a Market Yard shopkeeper who was travelling home with ₹4 lakh when the two men allegedly attempted to rob him.
 The attempt was unsuccessful after a young woman intervened and helped save the shopkeeper and his cash, according to the report. During questioning, the two suspects told Swargate police that they had robbed an Angadia of ₹35 lakh in the Market Yard area on October 9.
 Swargate police then linked the disclosure to the earlier complaint involving the businessman. The investigation led to the recovery of ₹25 lakh from the suspects, Kumar said. The reported recovery also brought the handling of the original complaint at Market Yard police station to the commissioner’s attention.
 The case highlights the importance of accurate first reporting in urban policing. The classification given at a police station determines how an incident is formally recorded, investigated and tracked. In this instance, the difference between a robbery case and a property-missing case delayed the identification of the alleged offence until information emerged from another police station’s investigation.
 The commissioner’s decision to transfer the senior inspector represents administrative action following the reported recording of the case. The supplied report does not state whether further disciplinary proceedings or an independent inquiry have been ordered. It also does not provide details of the identities of the suspects, the businessman or the Angadia involved.
 The next steps will depend on the investigation by Swargate police and the action taken by Pune Police over the handling of the original complaint. The reported recovery of ₹25 lakh leaves ₹10 lakh of the alleged ₹35 lakh robbery unaccounted for in the information supplied to the Times of India.
